blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has severe eczema, food allergies, markedly elevated IgE, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, and extensive molluscum contagiosum and herpes simplex skin infections. Platelet count and platelet size are normal. In a three-dimensional collagen matrix, his activated T cells become abnormally elongated and fragment during migration.
item.lead_in: Which cellular defect most directly explains the abnormal migration-survival phenotype?

options.B: Failure of DOCK8-dependent CDC42-PAK signaling that coordinates cytoskeletal structures during confined lymphocyte migration
options.C: Loss of WASp causing defective actin polymerization with microthrombocytopenia
options.D: Failure of phagocyte NADPH oxidase to generate superoxide
options.E: Loss of Bruton tyrosine kinase signaling in B-cell precursors

item.tested_construct: DOCK8-dependent CDC42-PAK control of lymphocyte shape integrity during migration through confined three-dimensional tissues
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: DOCK8-deficient T and NK cells can elongate, undergo nuclear deformation, and fragment during migration through confined collagen-rich spaces. Experimental loss of DOCK8 or CDC42 and inhibition or knockdown of PAK1/2 reproduce this shape-integrity and survival defect, whereas loss of WASp does not. Thus the migration-survival phenotype is most directly explained by failure of the DOCK8-CDC42-PAK axis that coordinates cytoskeletal structures during cell movement.

distractor_explanations.A: STAT3 deficiency can cause a hyper-IgE phenotype, but it does not explain the characteristic confined-migration elongation and cytothripsis phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. DOCK8 acts through CDC42 and PAK1/2 to preserve lymphocyte shape integrity during confined migration; disruption produces elongation, nuclear deformation, and cytothripsis.
distractor_explanations.C: WASp deficiency disrupts actin biology and causes Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, but experimental WASp loss did not reproduce the DOCK8-like elongation and cytothripsis phenotype; classic disease also features microthrombocytopenia.
distractor_explanations.D: NADPH oxidase deficiency causes defective phagocyte oxidative killing rather than a T-cell shape-integrity defect during three-dimensional migration.
distractor_explanations.E: BTK deficiency impairs B-cell maturation and immunoglobulin production rather than causing this hyper-IgE, cutaneous-viral, migration-fragmentation phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect DOCK8 loss to failure of CDC42-PAK-dependent coordination of cytoskeletal structures, causing lymphocyte elongation and cytothripsis during migration through confined tissues.

second_answer_attack.resolution: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is the strongest alternative because WASp affects actin and shares eczema and infection susceptibility, but the primary confined-migration experiment found that WASp loss did not reproduce the elongation/cytothripsis phenotype, while DOCK8, CDC42, and PAK1/2 perturbation did; normal platelet size and count further argue against classic WAS.
